Tomato___Early_blight.solution: Remove infected leaves and apply fungicides such as chlorothalonil or copper-based sprays. Rotate crops every season.
Tomato___Early_blight.reason: Early blight is caused by the fungus Alternaria solani which thrives in warm humid environments and spreads through infected soil and plant debris.

Tomato___Late_blight.solution: Apply copper-based fungicides immediately and remove infected plants. Ensure proper air circulation and avoid overhead watering.
Tomato___Late_blight.reason: Late blight is caused by the pathogen Phytophthora infestans which spreads rapidly in cool and moist conditions.

Tomato___healthy.solution: No treatment required. Maintain good irrigation practices and balanced fertilization.
Tomato___healthy.reason: The plant shows no visible symptoms of disease.

Potato___Early_blight.solution: Apply fungicides and remove infected leaves. Practice crop rotation and maintain proper spacing between plants.
Potato___Early_blight.reason: Early blight in potatoes is caused by Alternaria solani fungus which spreads in warm and humid conditions.

Potato___Late_blight.solution: Use resistant potato varieties and apply copper-based fungicides regularly.
Potato___Late_blight.reason: Late blight is caused by the pathogen Phytophthora infestans and spreads rapidly in wet weather.

Apple___Apple_scab.solution: Apply fungicides during the growing season and remove infected leaves from the ground.
Apple___Apple_scab.reason: Apple scab is caused by the fungus Venturia inaequalis which spreads through rain splash and wind.

Apple___Black_rot.solution: Prune infected branches and apply fungicide sprays during the growing season.
Apple___Black_rot.reason: Black rot is caused by the fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa which spreads through wounds in the tree.

Corn___Common_rust.solution: Plant resistant corn varieties and apply fungicides if the infection is severe.
Corn___Common_rust.reason: Corn rust is caused by the fungus Puccinia sorghi which spreads through airborne spores.

Tomato___Target_Spot.solution: Remove infected leaves, improve air circulation, avoid overhead watering, and apply appropriate fungicides such as chlorothalonil or copper-based sprays.
Tomato___Target_Spot.reason: Target Spot is caused by the fungus Corynespora cassiicola. It develops in warm, humid conditions and spreads through infected plant debris and water splash.
